endings.title: The Golden Cage
epilogue: You took Celeste's sponsorship and the title that came with it. The Corvane money kept flowing, and every quarter you signed a risk report you knew was incomplete.
Two years later an auditor from a client found Schedule 4. Your name was on the sponsorship email. The board asked for your resignation the same afternoon.

endings.title: The Clean Sweep
epilogue: The Corvane scheme ended in a courtroom, not a cover-up. Valtren recovered most of the money, the regulator praised the board's response, and the override route was closed for good.
Under your leadership the risk function became the place people bring bad news early. Dame Helen calls it the best thing that happened to Valtren in a decade.

endings.title: The Costly Truth
epilogue: You exposed the Corvane scheme, but the years of incidents had already cost Valtren its standing. The fraud was the headline; the weak controls were the story underneath.
You spend your first year as CRO rebuilding trust one honest report at a time. It is slow work, and it is working.

endings.title: The Truth Teller
epilogue: The Courier ran the story and the scheme collapsed within a week. Celeste left, and so did two directors who had looked away.
Some colleagues see you as the person who forced the truth out; others as the person who went to the press instead of the board. Both are right, and you know it.

endings.title: Quiet Money
epilogue: Celeste left with a settlement and a non-disclosure agreement. The share price never noticed.
The regulator did, eventually. When the Authority asked why a known fraud was never reported, the minutes showed whose recommendation the board had followed.

endings.title: Steady Hands
epilogue: No scandals, no heroics: just a company that saw its risks coming and dealt with them. Clients renew, the regulator visits less, and the board trusts the numbers.
Somewhere in the procurement files a supplier contract still has a page nobody has read. Perhaps your successor will find it.

endings.title: The Survivor
epilogue: You made it to the top of a company that took too many hits on the way. The incident log reads like a list of lessons learned the hard way.
The board gives you one job: make sure the next decade is quieter than the last.

endings.title: Chief Risk Officer
epilogue: From a stale warning at Northgate to the boardroom. You learned that risk management is not saying no; it is helping people say yes with their eyes open.
Valtren's risks are yours to lead now.
